title: The Sharp Gray Sheep (Scotland)

full_text:
In the misty Scottish Highlands lived an earl's daughter whose gentle mother died, leaving her to the malice of an unjust stepmother.
The stepmother dressed the maiden in rough homespun wool, sent her to herd sheep on the windy moors, and gave her only a thimbleful of coarse oatcake to sustain her throughout the day.

Among the flock was a remarkable Sharp Gray Sheep that had belonged to her mother.
Seeing the maiden weeping from cold and hunger, the sheep spoke:
'Weep not, my lassie. Prick my right ear with a silver bodkin, and take what thou findest.'
The maiden touched the ear, and out rolled a snow-white linen cloth filled with warm bannocks, sweet butter, and fresh curd cheese. She ate, gave thanks, and was comforted.

The stepmother, seeing the maiden growing healthy and strong despite starvation, sent her own daughter to spy on the moors, discovering the secret.
The cruel woman demanded the Sharp Gray Sheep be slaughtered for dinner.
Before the knife fell, the sheep whispered:
'Gather my bones from the hearth ash; bury them under the flat stone beside the burn, and whatever thou hast need of, ask.'

The maiden buried the bones by the stream.
When the King's son rode through the glen to choose a bride at the church of the kirkyard, the stepmother locked the maiden in the pantry.
The maiden slipped through the window, ran to the burn, and tapped the stone.
The stone opened, giving her a dress of spun golden thistles and slippers of finest glass!

At the kirk, the Prince could not look away from her radiant grace. As she slipped away across the stepping stones, her glass slipper was left upon the heather.
The Prince tested every foot in the Highlands until he reached the earl's house.
The maiden stepped forward from the pantry, the glass shoe embraced her foot with ease, and the burnished golden gown reappeared!
The Prince carried her to his castle, where she ruled as a beloved lady of the glens, forever remembering the quiet stream that guarded her mother’s love.
moral: Ancestral love leaves living blessings; natural harmony preserves the innocent against malice.
